scenario: AITA for not wanting to share an animal crossing town with my girlfriend? | This is kind of petty but here goes. The new animal crossing game is coming out and you can only have one village per nintendo switch console. my girlfriend and I both have a switch, but she wants to share one village with me so were both using one switch to play. I told her I would rather us both get the game so we can play online and customize our towns the way we want to, but she disagreed. I even told her I would buy her the game but she said she wants to feel a sense of "togetherness" in animal crossing which I just dont get. When I insisted we play on different consoles, even with valid reasoning and all that, she stormed out. called me an asshole baby, and told me to grow up. Animal crossing is a beloved series for me and I want to be able to make my village the way I want to, and I would also like to be able to play with my girlfriend online. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to not want to share an Animal Crossing town with their girlfriend. Let me break this down step by step. First, I know that Animal Crossing is a game where you can create and customize your own village. It's a pretty personal thing because you get to design your town exactly how you like it. So, if someone really loves the series and wants to make their village the way they want, that makes sense. On the other hand, the girlfriend wants to feel a sense of "togetherness" by sharing one village. She probably thinks that playing together in the same town would make their relationship stronger and more connected. But the guy in this situation doesn't understand why she feels that way. He wants to play on different consoles so he can customize his town as he likes and also play online with her. Now, is it right or wrong for him to not want to share the town? Well, I think it depends on how both people feel about it. If one person feels strongly about something, it's important to respect that. But at the same time, communication is key. They should talk about why they feel the way they do and try to find a compromise. In this case, the guy offered to buy her the game so they can both have their own towns. That seems like a fair solution because they can still play together online and customize their own villages. But the girlfriend refused, wanting to share one town for the sense of togetherness. Maybe the issue is that they have different priorities. He values the customization and personalization of his town, while she values the shared experience. It's not necessarily right or wrong, but it's about finding a balance that works for both of them. I also think about how they communicate. The girlfriend stormed out and called him names, which isn't helpful. It's important to express feelings without attacking the other person. Maybe they need to have a calmer conversation to understand each other's perspectives better. In the end, it's about mutual respect and finding a middle ground. If they can't agree, maybe they need to consider whether this is a deal-breaker or if there are other ways to compromise. But ultimately, both should feel heard and respected in the relationship.
